From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Chen <claire@medtechai.com>, Tom Sullivan <tom.sullivan@medtechai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP draft: Data handling & compliance (retention, logging, PHI/PII constraints) - post-demo recap

Hi Claire / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the call earlier. Thanks for walking through the MedTech AI use case — the team and I took a few notes and sketched an initial MAP milestone focused on Data Handling & Compliance. I attached a draft MAP (MAP-v1.1.xlsx) and a short SOC2 evidence request doc for your legal/security review.

High-level summary of the Data Handling & Compliance MAP milestone:

- Goal: Define and agree controls for retention, logging/audit, and PHI/PII constraints to enable a pilot that meets your compliance needs.
- Target close date: 2026-03-15 (open to negotiation based on procurement/legal timelines)
- Responsibilities:
  - MedTech AI (Claire/Tom): provide data classification, examples of records that may contain PHI/PII, and procurement timeline.
  - Redwood (Aditya/Marissa): provide SOC2 artifacts, BAA template, technical constraints for avoiding persistent storage of PHI, and an implementation plan for audit logs and retention controls.
- Key dependencies: legal review (BAA), SOC2 artifact review, procurement PO/contract, and our engineering scoping on prompt redaction and retention windows.
- Initial ask from you: confirm whether MedTech AI will send PHI to Redwood for inference during pilot, and if so the minimal retention/window requirements for audit and regulatory needs.

Notes on capabilities (short):
- Storage/retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies per-customer and per-route; we can set short retention windows for request/response logs and a longer retention for audit trail entries as required by the customer.
- Logging/audit: we provide immutable audit trails for request metadata (timestamp, route, model, requester id) and can surface access logs to your SIEM via secure delivery or API.
- PHI/PII: we do not require customers to send PHI; if customers choose to, we offer options to avoid persistent storage of raw prompts (ephemeral-only processing), field-level redaction guidance, and encryption-in-transit and at-rest using customer-managed KMS.

Attachments: MAP-v1.1.xlsx (draft milestones + responsibility matrix), SOC2-evidence-request.docx (list of artifacts legal/security often asks for), BAA-template.pdf (for legal to start).

Next steps / Proposed:
1) Claire: confirm whether pilot will include PHI and share any regulatory retention needs (e.g., state/local requirements) by EOD 2/13.
2) Redwood (Marissa/Logan): send SOC2 evidence and BAA template and scope a short technical note on how we can avoid storing PHI by 2/14.
3) Align on target close date for MAP milestone after legal/procurement input (we suggested 2026-03-15).

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync if useful.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: MAP draft: Data handling & compliance (retention, logging, PHI/PII constraints) - post-demo recap

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear MAP. A few clarifications from our side:

- PHI: For the pilot we expect to process de-identified PHI and in some cases limited direct identifiers. We cannot store direct identifiers long-term; we need a workflow that ensures prompts containing direct identifiers are either redacted before persistence or not persisted at all.
- Retention: For audit purposes we need an immutable access log for 7 years for certain records; however raw prompts containing identifiers should not be retained beyond ephemeral processing unless explicitly approved.
- BAA/SOC2: Please share the BAA and SOC2-related artifacts as soon as possible. Our legal team will want to review the BAA and may request a few minor clauses for state-specific controls.

Also looping Tom (procurement) — Tom, can you share the procurement timeline and send the procurement contact? We aim to have internal legal + procurement sign-off within 3–4 weeks if we can get the BAA and SOC2 artifacts this week.

Thanks Aditya — looping in the right owners and proposing owners for the MAP items below. Quick notes & assignments based on Claire's reply:

- Marissa (me) -> send SOC2 artifacts + SOC2 evidence request doc to Claire's legal team by EOD 2/14. I will attach the docs and include a short readme describing where each artifact comes from.
- Logan (cc) -> legal/technical SME on PHI handling and redaction options. Logan, can you draft a ~1 page technical note on:
  * options for ephemeral-only processing (no persistence of raw prompts),
  * field-level redaction guidance for common medical identifiers, and
  * how we surface immutable audit logs and deliver them to customer SIEM/S3. Target: 2/16.
- Aditya -> update MAP with the clarified responsibilities and push tentative target close date to 2026-03-22 to give legal/procurement runway.

Attachments I'm sending now: SOC2-evidence-request.docx (full artifact list), BAA-template.pdf (copy of our standard).

Dependencies:
- Claire / MedTech: confirm whether any state-specific PHI retention rules apply that would change the 7-year access log ask.
- Procurement: need PO/contract timeline from Tom so we can finalize target close date.

Aditya — once Logan's technical note is ready, I'll combine everything into MAP-v1.2 and send to Claire/Legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
